name: Sporadic Porphyria Cutanea Tarda

criteria.description: Elevated uroporphyrin and other porphyrins in urine
Evidence of hepatic iron overload by biopsy or imaging
Characteristic photosensitive blistering skin lesions on sun-exposed areas
Reduced uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase enzyme activity in liver or erythrocytes
No family history of porphyria (distinguishing sporadic from familial forms)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cutaneous blistering with elevated urinary porphyrins and reduced UROD enzyme activity or hepatic iron overload
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by exclusion of familial forms and confirmation of biochemical abnormalities.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Photosensitive vesicles and bullae on dorsal hands
pathognomonic.notes: Blistering occurs on sun-exposed skin, especially dorsal hands and forearms
searchTerms: blisters on back of hands from sun
vesicles and bullae on dorsal hands

pathognomonic.symptomName: Skin fragility with erosions and crusting
pathognomonic.notes: Skin is fragile and prone to trauma-induced erosions

common.symptomName: Hypertrichosis on the face and forearms
common.notes: Excessive hair growth, especially on cheeks and forearms
searchTerms: excess hair growth on face and arms
too much hair on forearms and face

common.symptomName: Milia formation on healed skin lesions
common.notes: Small white cysts develop at sites of previous blistering
searchTerms: small white bumps on healed skin

common.notes: Chronic lesions lead to scarring and skin atrophy
searchTerms: skin that tears easily and scars

common.notes: Mild to moderate elevation of ALT and AST common
Non-specific systemic symptoms may be present

searchTerms: skin that feels tight and firm

occasional.notes: Enlarged liver detected on physical exam or imaging
Occasional mild icterus due to liver dysfunction

rare.notes: Advanced liver disease in chronic cases

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms such as peripheral neuropathy

searchTerms: blisters on skin not exposed to sun
photosensitivity causing blisters in covered areas
skin blistering triggered by light on non-sun areas

laboratory: Elevated urinary uroporphyrin and heptacarboxyl porphyrins
Increased plasma porphyrins with characteristic fluorescence peak
Elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation
imaging: Liver ultrasound or MRI showing iron overload
Liver biopsy demonstrating iron deposition and reduced UROD activity
other: Positive plasma fluorescence emission peak at 620 nm
Improvement with phlebotomy or low-dose hydroxychloroquine therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Blistering on trauma-prone areas without photosensitivity
Similar blistering but normal porphyrin studies
Associated with drug exposure or renal failure

redFlags: Rapidly progressive blistering with systemic symptoms
Signs of liver failure or hepatic encephalopathy
